rule_based_system.summary: An ordered list of IF-THEN rules over grounded market predicates; the first rule that fires decides, with its training up-rate.
rule_based_system.implementationNote: Bridge: first-match decision list; P(up) is the fired rule's smoothed training up-rate (default rule: the base rate), calibrated on validation. Differs from the spec: authored TA rules from cycle_rules.json plus rules mined on the training span, since no expert rule base exists for this market. Expect: coarse, step-like probabilities; coverage depends on how often the rules fire.

induced_feature_count.label: Induced feature predicates
induced_feature_count.description: Feature columns turned into two predicates each (above the training 2/3 quantile, below the 1/3 quantile), chosen by how differently their tails moved on the training span.

atom_order.label: Conditions per mined rule
atom_order.description: Largest number of predicates in one mined rule (1: single conditions, 2: pairs).

minimum_fire_count.label: Minimum firings
minimum_fire_count.description: A mined rule must have fired on at least this many training bars.

rule_count.label: Rules kept
rule_count.description: Rules kept after ranking by how far their training up-rate sits from the base rate.

smoothing_pseudo_count.label: Smoothing pseudo-count
smoothing_pseudo_count.description: Pseudo-bars at the base rate added to every training rate (Laplace-style smoothing).

expert_system.summary: Forward chaining over a working memory of graded facts with MYCIN certainty factors: pattern rules assert setups, hypothesis rules turn them into belief in an up move.
expert_system.implementationNote: Bridge: MYCIN forward chaining (recognise-act cycles, refraction, certainty combination); the final certainty of 'up' is mapped to P(up) by a validation curve. Differs from the spec: rule certainty factors are calibrated on the training span (MB/MD from training up-rates) instead of elicited from an expert. Expect: probabilities near the base rate unless strong patterns fire together.

certainty_threshold.label: Certainty threshold
certainty_threshold.description: A rule fires only when its premise certainty is at least this (MYCIN uses 0.2).

maximum_inference_cycles.label: Inference cycles
maximum_inference_cycles.description: Recognise-act cycles before inference stops (two are needed to reach a hypothesis).

probabilistic_logic_network.summary: Truth values with strength and evidence count; implication links from predicates to an up move are chained by PLN deduction and merged by revision.
probabilistic_logic_network.implementationNote: Bridge: PLN deduction and revision over training-span truth values; P(up) = confidence x strength + (1 - confidence) x base rate, then a validation curve. Differs from the spec: atoms are the bar's grounded predicates and concepts are mined rules, not an AtomSpace; deduction assumes independent links. Expect: estimates close to the base rate when evidence is thin.

evidence_scale.label: Evidence scale
evidence_scale.description: k in confidence = n / (n + k): how many observations make a link trustworthy.

maximum_chain_depth.label: Chain depth
maximum_chain_depth.description: 1: direct links only; 2: one deduction through a concept; 3: through two concepts.

probabilistic_soft_logic.summary: Weighted soft-logic rules over [0, 1] predicate truths define a hinge-loss energy; the truth of 'up' is its exact minimiser, with weights learned by the structured perceptron.
probabilistic_soft_logic.implementationNote: Bridge: exact MAP of a one-variable hinge-loss MRF (Lukasiewicz rules, up/down mutual exclusion); P(up) is a validation curve of the MAP truth. Differs from the spec: one free atom per bar, so no ADMM is needed; rules come from the shared predicate library. Expect: behaves like a learned soft rule vote.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.description: Step size of each weight update.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay
weight_decay.description: Shrinks every rule weight toward zero each epoch.

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Epochs without validation improvement before stopping.

fuzzy_logic_model.summary: Linguistic terms (low / medium / high) on the most informative features, Wang-Mendel rules learned from training bars, Mamdani min-max inference and centroid defuzzification.
fuzzy_logic_model.implementationNote: Bridge: vectorised Mamdani inference (checked against scikit-fuzzy's control system); the centroid bullishness in [-1, 1] becomes P(up) through a validation curve. Differs from the spec: rules are generated from training bars (Wang-Mendel), not written by hand. Expect: smooth but low-resolution scores.

input_feature_count.label: Inputs
input_feature_count.description: Feature columns used as fuzzy inputs (most training mutual information).

rule_count.label: Rules kept
rule_count.description: Wang-Mendel rules kept, by training degree mass.

defuzzification_grid_points.label: Defuzzification grid
defuzzification_grid_points.description: Points of the output universe the centroid is computed on.

first_order_logic.summary: A quantified Horn knowledge base over lookback windows (trend, alignment, confirmation) proved per bar by resolution refutation with unification.
first_order_logic.implementationNote: Bridge: the strongest conclusion proved per direction (confirmed, aligned, leaning, none) indexes a table of training up-rates, calibrated on validation. Differs from the spec: the spec proves entailment; P(up) is the train-span up-rate of its output, calibrated on validation, and quantification runs over lookback windows, not instruments. Expect: few distinct cells, so coarse probabilities.
first_order_logic.estimatedTrainingTime: under a minute per fold (proofs are memoised)

logic_programming.summary: A Prolog-style program of trend, support and rule clauses answered by SLD resolution (miniKanren); the model counts distinct derivations of a long and a short signal.
logic_programming.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is a validation curve of (derivations of signal(up) - derivations of signal(down)). Differs from the spec: Prolog proves, it does not estimate, so the derivation count is the bridge; miniKanren stands in for SWI-Prolog. Expect: a vote-like score near the base rate.
logic_programming.estimatedTrainingTime: under a minute per fold (answers are tabled)

constraint_satisfaction.summary: The bar's side (long or short) under hard constraints from high-confidence rules (solved by python-constraint) and weighted soft constraints from reliable predicates.
constraint_satisfaction.implementationNote: Bridge: score = soft-CSP cost of short minus cost of long (violated weights plus an infeasibility penalty), calibrated on validation. Differs from the spec: the spec checks feasibility; P(up) is the train-span up-rate of its output, calibrated on validation, with one decision variable per bar and no portfolio sizing. Expect: probabilities near the base rate.

fuzzy_decision_model.summary: A first-order Takagi-Sugeno system: Gaussian terms on the most informative features, Wang-Mendel rules with linear consequents, tuned by ANFIS hybrid learning.
fuzzy_decision_model.implementationNote: Bridge: the TSK output (+1 up / -1 down target) becomes P(up) through a validation curve; the price model is the same system fitted to the scaled move. Differs from the spec: rules are learned from training bars, inputs capped so rules stay populated. Expect: a smooth, locally linear score.

multi_criteria_decision_analysis.summary: TOPSIS: the current bar ranked against its trailing window on the most informative signals, weighted by the analytic hierarchy process or entropy.
multi_criteria_decision_analysis.implementationNote: Bridge: the bar's TOPSIS closeness to the ideal (0..1) minus 0.5, calibrated on validation; the price model scales it by a training slope. Differs from the spec: the spec ranks alternatives; here each bar is ranked against training-span ideals (or its trailing window) and P(up) is the calibrated up-rate of that rank. Expect: a weighted composite signal.

criterion_count.label: Criteria
criterion_count.description: Feature columns with the largest training information coefficient.

ideal_reference.label: Ideal reference
ideal_reference.description: Rank the bar against the training span's 5th-95th percentile ideals, or against its own trailing window (fixed: it sets the history requirement).

sequence_length.label: Trailing alternatives
sequence_length.description: Bars in the trailing decision matrix when the ideal reference is the trailing window, the current one included (fixed: it sets the history requirement).

weighting_method.label: Weighting
weighting_method.description: Criterion weights from AHP pairwise ratios of information coefficients, or the entropy method.

robust_decision_making.summary: A pool of candidate strategies stress-tested across training-span scenarios (blocks, volatility terciles, trend regimes, doubled costs); the robust ones are blended.
robust_decision_making.implementationNote: Bridge: the robustness-weighted blend of the surviving strategies' scores, calibrated on validation. Differs from the spec: scenarios are re-cuts of the training history with cost stress, so deep uncertainty is only as deep as that history. Expect: a conservative ensemble near the base rate.

candidate_strategy_count.label: Candidate strategies
candidate_strategy_count.description: Strategies in the pool (single features, a logistic regression and three rule strategies).

scenario_block_count.label: Scenario blocks
scenario_block_count.description: Contiguous blocks the training span is cut into.

acceptable_utility_threshold.label: Acceptable utility
acceptable_utility_threshold.description: Mean net utility (scaled move units per bar) a scenario outcome must reach to satisfice.

robustness_metric.label: Robustness metric
robustness_metric.description: Share of scenarios satisficed, or the worst regret against each scenario's best strategy.

scenario_discovery_depth.label: Scenario discovery depth
scenario_discovery_depth.description: Depth of the tree that describes where the robust set fails.
